\section{Results}
\subsection{Sample}
After excluding 140 students who moved during the school year,
the final analysis sample comprises 5,240 students in 60 schools,
balanced across treatment and control arms on baseline covariates.

\subsection{Main Estimates}
The encouragement to reduce class size by eight students raises
standardized reading scores by 2.9 points (standard error 0.8)
after one year, significant at the one percent level.
Effects are concentrated in schools with above-median baseline
class sizes.

\subsection{Costs}
The additional teaching allocations cost \$210 per student per year,
implying a cost-effectiveness ratio that compares favourably with
tutoring programmes of similar duration.

\subsection{Robustness}
Estimates are stable to alternative inference procedures and to
dropping schools with partial compliance.
